newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-Britain mourns humiliating Zimbabwe cricket loss.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Britain mourns humiliating Zimbabwe cricket loss.

text.p: British newspapers solemnly lined up on Saturday to read the last rites for their national cricket team after a mortifying defeat by part-timers in distant and dusty Zimbabwe.

"English cricket collapsed and died yesterday, aged 120," intoned the Daily Express. "As is usual with such tragedies abroad, a post-mortem will be held, but the cause of death is understood to be simple: humiliation."

Broadsheets and tabloids agreed that, even judged by the team's current indifferent standards, Friday's loss spearheaded by chicken farmer Eddo Brandes represented a new low for the country which gave birth to the sport.

"The England cricket team were laid low yesterday by a chicken farmer from Zimbabwe in what must rank as one of the nation's most humiliating defeats of all time," the Independent said in a front-page article.

As if to rub in the extent of England's general decline, the paper printed a map showing that an empire which once covered a third of the world had been reduced to a scattered handful of small islands and protectorates.

England had already lost the previous two one-day games to Zimbabwe before Friday's match but the gutless nature of the defeat prompted many commentators to call for the team to be summoned home instead of going on to New Zealand.
"The nation that invented cricket has been well and truly plucked," said the tabloid Daily Mirror, which published a front-page lament "for our cricket flops."

The Daily Telegraph likened the loss to a public flogging, while the downmarket Sun ran a six-page "disaster special" featuring a damning interview with 19th century cricketing hero W.G. Grace -- carried out through a medium.
There were few outbursts of anger in the press, reflecting an increasingly popular belief that captain Michael Atherton and his players are beyond redemption.
"Laughter and ridicule are the only means of preserving sanity when talking about the England cricket team," said the Sun, which printed a photo of a sheep bearing Atherton's face.

"Our reputation as a cricketing nation has been shot to pieces in Zimbabwe. Now we are heading for New Zealand like lambs to the slaughter," said the Mirror, who made up Atherton to look like one of Walt Disney's seven dwarves.

"If Atherton didn't captain the worst team in the world last year, he's streets ahead in 1997," it added. "Back home the needles are falling off our Christmas trees while the wheels fall off our shambling parody of a team in Zimbabwe."
